# Catching Heap Buffer Overflows with AddressSanitizer

## Thesis

**AddressSanitizer (ASan)** turns silent memory corruption into a loud, actionable report. You compile with `-fsanitize=address`, keep frame pointers, and run the binary — redzones around heap objects catch overflows that MPX-style hardware bounds checks often missed in practice. This chapter deliberately overflows a four-`int` allocation and reads the report.

## Mental model

```text
  malloc(16)  →  [redzone][ 16 bytes ][redzone]
                              ▲
                         p[4] write lands in redzone → ASan trap
```

| Flag | Why |
|------|-----|
| `-fsanitize=address` | Link the runtime and instrument loads/stores |
| `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` | Readable stacks in reports |
| `-O0` or `-O1` | Keep the bug visible; `-O2` can elide dead stores |

Intel **MPX** tried hardware bounds tables; it was removed from Linux and GCC because of cost and incomplete coverage. ASan stays the boring CI default for C/C++ memory bugs.

## Worked examples

Verified with **gcc** + `libasan.so.8` on Linux/amd64.

### Case 1: heap buffer overflow

```c
// oob.c
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) {
  volatile int *p = (volatile int *)malloc(4 * sizeof(int));
  if (!p) return 1;
  p[4] = 42; /* deliberate OOB write */
  printf("survived? %d\n", p[0]);
  free((void *)p);
  return 0;
}
```

```bash
cc -O0 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -o oob oob.c
./oob
```

## Trap

**Shipping ASan builds to production.** The runtime is for tests and fuzzing. It enlarges memory and slows code. Keep it on in CI and in canary fuzz jobs; strip it from release binaries.

## Boring rule

Every C PR that touches unsafe buffers gets an ASan (and preferably UBSan) CI job. Reproduce with a 10-line file before arguing about "theoretical" bugs.

## Try this

1. Change the bug to a **use-after-free** (`free` then write) and compare the report.
2. Add `-fsanitize=undefined` and trip a signed overflow.
3. Run the same binary under Valgrind and compare the wording (slower, no recompile).
